To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Facebook use is driven by disconnection, but that it also rewards connection, and that disconnection motivated greater Facebook use during a subsequent 48-hr Facebook-free period.

(a) Facebook use is motivated by a desire to feel connected, and use leads to feeling more connected, and (b) Facebook use is also motivated by a desire for disconnection, and use leads, paradoxically, to feeling more disconnected.
(a) people use Facebook in part to cope with feelings of social disconnection and that (b) this use is rewarding, in part, when it leads to feelings of connection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether Facebook use can help users to meet their needs for relatedness, and our answer is that it can, but not in the way one might initially expect.
the question of how Facebook is used to meet psychological needs.
the paradox of why people who are more disconnected from other people use more Facebook.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
disconnection motivators use and connection rewards it.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Facebook use is a two-process coping strategy: people turn to it to satisfy their need to belong (connection), and they turn away from it when they are disconnected (disconnection).
the use of social networking sites (SNSs) can have positive and negative consequences on people's well-being, and that the use of SNSs may be motivated by the need to feel connected to others.
Facebook is used for both connection and disconnection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the more people feel disconnected from others, the more they will use Facebook as a coping strategy.
the need for relatedness can be satisfied by Facebook use, but that the use of Facebook can be motivated by a sense of relatedness deficiency.
the more people use Facebook to connect with others, the better they feel, and the more they use Facebook.
